decisions: Option A accepted (didOpen on-query, scoped to java_diagnostics): the daemon composition root (src/cli.ts) sends textDocument/didOpen for the queried document before a file-scoped java_diagnostics answer and waits for its publishDiagnostics within the call deadline. Adds INV-DIAG-4 to harness/docs/design/tool-surface.md; src/tools/diagnostics.ts keeps its 'never sends an LSP request' invariant (the didOpen is a daemon-side wiring side effect, not a tool-layer request).

Option B (readiness gate additionally waits for diagnostics) rejected: it mixes a per-file concern (publishDiagnostics for one URI) into a per-workspace gate and muddies INV-READY-2 (readiness decided by semantic probe, never by status).
Option C (file-sync-watcher opens every Java file on watch) rejected: O(files) didOpen on startup, memory/time cost, overkill for single-file queries.
Prior decision (Option R, project-router reactor-root resolution, approvedBy truong.hn.1994@gmail.com on 2026-08-21) remains in force and is recorded in DECISIONS.md.
acceptedRisks: didOpen -> publishDiagnostics is asynchronous: if the publish does not arrive by the call deadline, java_diagnostics still answers 'not-reported' (an honest fallback under INV-DIAG-1), never a hang — the bounded wait respects the per-call deadline budget (X-001).

<modules> tag detection is validated only against the current fixture tree, not an independent Maven-model parser — an atypical multi-module layout could be misclassified (carried over from the 2026-08-21 approval).
